Grape Soda

Amt Ingred
400g Purple seedy (Concord?) grapes- the ones with flavour, not the red sugar balls grapes from the store
200g Sugar
2L Water
1/8tsp Molasses
1/4tsp Pectic enzyme

Directions: Start yeast in a splash of water, sugar and the molasses. Blend fruit, 500mL water, and pectic enzyme and let stand for 48 hours. Mix sugar and remaining water in fermenting vessel and strain in the juice/pulp mix. Add yeast starter. When the yeast is visibly active, bottle the mash/must and refrigerate once pressurized.

Improved method for fruit/berry sodas: no simmering, extract flavour with time and pectic enzyme.

Prior attempts, carrying over from ginger beer, had me extracting flavour with simmering, sometimes for a long time. As mentioned in prior posts, this was a problem because of the pectin that was also extracted and that clumped and formed long lasting foam. I countered with pectic enzyme but the flavour was harmed.

Taking the advice of winemakers, I scrapped simmering entirely and blended up the grapes with the pectic enzyme to break down the fruit flesh and extract the juice and flavour. I let the enzyme work for nearly 48 hours at room temperature, after which I strained and squished the pulp through a cloth filter I made to fit my funnel. Squishing, while pushing through more solids and creating haze and sediment, easily doubled the amount of juice (and flavour!) recovered. All told, there is barely any sediment so I definitely recommend gently squishing juice out of the pulp if using a fine filter.

The mash/must tasted really good. The grape flavour is much milder than, for example, store bought grape juice, and as you can see the colour is vastly different. I forgot to add lemon juice for acidity but I don't think it is needed; the flavour is at first acidic and seems headed toward very tart territory but stops as soon as it hits the palate. Then the sweet grape notes come forward.
